questions.question: A and B entered into a business with initial investments of Rs. 2000 and Rs. 1875 respectively and the ratio of time for which they made their investments is 5:4 respectively. Find profit share of A if total profit earned by both of them is Rs. 3276.
questions.explanation:
According to question,

Ratio of profit share of A and B = (2000 × 5): (1875 × 4) = 4:3

Profit share of A = \(\frac{4}{7}\) × 3276 = Rs. 1872

Hence, option c.

questions.question: Mohan and Sohan start a business with an investment of Rs 80000 and Rs. 120000 for 8 months and 18 months respectively and Sohan gets Rs. 8100 at the end of the year. Then, find the profit of Mohan?
questions.explanation:
Profit = Investment × time
Mohan’s profit = 80000 × 8 = 64000
Sohan’s profit = 120000 × 18 = 216000
Ratio of their profit = 64000 : 216000 = 8 : 27

Mohan's profit =810027×8= Rs. 2400

questions.question: P and Q started a retail store with initial investments in the ratio 5: 6 and their annual profits were in the ratio 2 : 3. If P invested the money for 8 months. For how many months did Q invest his money?
questions.explanation:
Suppose P invested Rs. 5x for 8 months and Q invested 6x for y months then,

\(\frac{5x \times 8}{6x \times y}\) =\(\frac{2}{3}\)

y=\(\frac{40x \times 3}{6x \times 2}\)

y=\(\frac{120x}{12x}\)

y = 10.

questions.question: P invested Rs. 5000 in a business and after 6 months, Q also joined him. At the end of year, Q received Rs. 2700 profit out of Rs. 8700. Find the investment of Q.
questions.explanation:
Let the investment of Q be Rs. x

profit received by P = 5000 × 12 = 60000

Profit received by Q = x ×  6 

Ratio of their profits = 10000 : x 

Profit received by Q at the end of the year = Rs. 2700 out of total profit of Rs. 8700

⇒ x/(10000 + x) × 8700 = 2700

⇒ 87x = 270000 + 27 x  

⇒ 60x = 270000

⇒ x = 4500

questions.question: Tanmay and Shivam started a business with investments of ₹5600 and ₹4200 respectively. After one year, Tanmay’s share of profit is ₹8400. Find the profit share of Shivam after one year.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Investment of Tanmay = ₹5600
  • Investment of Shivam = ₹4200
  • Time period = 1 year
  • Tanmay’s share of profit = ₹8400

Calculation:

Investment of Tanmay : Investment of Shivam
= 5600 : 4200
= 4 : 3

Since the time period is the same (1 year), the profit will be shared in the ratio of their investments.

Profit ratio = 4 : 3

Tanmay’s profit share = 8400

So, Shivam’s profit share
= 8400 × (3 / 4)
= 6300

Used Concept:

  • In partnership, profit is divided in the ratio of investments when time is same
  • Profit share ∝ Investment

questions.question: Ambuj starts a business with initial capital 'x' and after 1-year Mayank joins him with an initial capital of 'x + 3200'. If the ratio of profit share of Ambuj to Mayank at the end of 5 years is 15: 16, then what is the initial capital of Mayank?
questions.explanation:
Profit share of Ambuj = (x) x 5 = 5x
Profit share of Mayank = (x + 3200) x 4 = (4x + 12800)
Ratio of their profit = 5x: (4x + 12800) = 15 : 16

16x = 3(4x + 12800)
4x = 38400
x = 9600
Initial capital of Mayank = (x + 3200) = Rs.12800

questions.question: After investing Rs. 45,000 and Rs. 95,000 respectively in a business, X and Y want to know the ratio in which they should divide the profit between them at the end of two years. What should be the ratio of profit sharing between them?
questions.explanation:
Given:

X start a business by investing Rs. 45,000

Y start a business investing by Rs. 95,000,

Total time of investment = 2 years

Calculation:

Total amount invest by X in 2 years = 45000 × 2 = 90000

Total amount invest by Y in 2 years = 95000 × 2 = 190000

∴ Profit ration b/w X and Y after 2 years of their investment

= 90000 : 190000

= 9 : 19

questions.question: Ajay and Vijay started a business by investing in a ratio 5:9. Ajay invested the amount for the whole year while Vijay invested the amount for half year. Find the ratio in which profit is divided between them?
questions.explanation:
Solution (3)
Let the capital of Ajay \(( C 1)=5 x\)
And the capital of Vijay \(( C 2)=9 x\)
Time period spend by Ajay \(( T 1)=12\) months
Let, time period spend by Vijay \(( T 2)=6\) months
Apply formula: \(\frac{ C 1 \times T 1}{ C 2 \times T 2}=\frac{ P 1}{ P 2}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{5 x \times 12}{9 x \times 6}=\left(\frac{ P 1}{ P 2}\right) \\
& \frac{10}{9}=\left(\frac{ P 1}{ P 2}\right)
\end{aligned}
\]
the ratio in which profit is divided between them is \(10: 9\)

questions.question: P and Q enter into a partnership. P invests some money at the beginning, Q invests double the amount after four months, and R invests the amount thrice after eight months. If the annual profit is Rs.32000, R's share is?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • P, Q, and R enter a partnership.
  • P invests some amount (say ₹x) at the beginning.
  • Q invests double of P's amount (2x) after 4 months.
  • R invests triple of P's amount (3x) after 8 months.
  • Annual profit = ₹32,000
  • Find: R's share of the profit

Calculation:

Step 1 : Calculate the effective investment (Investment × Time)

P: ₹x for 12 months → 12x

Q: 2x for 8 months → 16x

R: 3x for 4 months → 12x

Step 2 : Total effective investment = 12x + 16x + 12x = 40x

Step 3: R's share
⇒R’s share = (R’s investment × time) ÷ Total × Profit

= 12x ÷ 40x × 32,000

= (12/40) × 32,000

= 0.3 × 32,000
= ₹9,600

R’s share = ₹9,600

Concept Used:

Profit in a partnership is distributed in proportion to the product of investment × time (in months) each partner’s money was invested.

questions.question: P started a business with ₹X. After 2 months, Q joined the business with ₹(X - 200) and after 5 more months, R joined the business with ₹(X + 1000). At the end of the year, out of total profit, Q’s profit share is ₹4000 and R’s profit share is ₹2500, then find P’s profit share?
questions.explanation:
At the end of the year, ratio between profit shares of P, Q and R respectively:

[X × 12]: [(X - 200) × 10]: [(X + 1000) × 5]

Since, ratio of Q’s profit share to R’s profit share:

4000: 2500 = 8: 5

So,

\(\frac{(X\  - \ 200)\  \times \ 10}{(X\  + \ 1000)\  \times \ 5}\  = \ \frac{8}{5}\)

5X - 1000 = 4X + 4000

X = 5000

Now, ratio P’s profit share to Q’s profit share:

[5000 × 12]: [(5000 - 200) × 10]

60000: 48000 = 5: 4

So, P’s profit share = \(4000\  \times \ \frac{5}{4}\) = ₹5000
